data.body_html:
Marbella's Feria San Bernabé 2026 (8–14 June) is the Costa del Sol's biggest summer kick-off – a week of fairground rides, flamenco, street parades, and nightly fireworks over the Mediterranean. Watching the fireworks from a private boat is the ultimate upgrade: no crowds, no traffic jams, and a front-row seat with a glass of cava in hand. This guide covers the best boats for the Feria, pricing, insider tips, and everything you need to plan your day on the water.

Why charter a yacht for Feria San Bernabé?

The Feria fairground is set along the seafront in central Marbella, so the fireworks launch directly over the water. From a boat anchored a few hundred metres offshore, you get a panoramic view of the whole display – plus the city lights reflecting on the sea. You avoid the packed promenade, the queues for taxis, and the noise of the crowds. Many guests charter a boat for a sunset cruise, drop anchor for the fireworks, then head back to Puerto Banús for dinner. It's the most relaxed way to experience Marbella's biggest party.

All our boats depart from Puerto Banús, a 10-minute taxi ride from the fairground. Here are the top options for Feria San Bernabé 2026:

Fireworks viewing: the best strategy

Fireworks start around 11 PM each night, with the grand finale on 14 June. Our recommendation: book a 2-hour charter from 10 PM to midnight. Depart Puerto Banús, cruise east along the coast (about 15–20 minutes), and anchor near the fairground. The captain will find the best spot. Bring a jacket – sea breezes cool down after sunset. The Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 are perfect for this: €749 for 2 hours, including drinks and snacks. You can also extend to 4 hours (€1,399) to include a pre-fireworks sunset cruise.

Daytime boat parties during the Feria

Many groups combine a daytime boat party with an evening at the fairground. The Mangusta 80 (€4,719 for 4 hours, 12 pax) includes a free jet ski – ideal for afternoon fun. You can cruise to Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés for a swim, then return to Puerto Banús by 5 PM to freshen up before heading to the Feria. For larger groups, the Ferretti 94 (29m) or Canados 86 (26m) offer spacious decks, a flybridge, and full crew service. Prices for these are on request – contact us via WhatsApp for a quote.

What's included – no surprises

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). There are no hidden fees. You can bring your own food or ask the crew to arrange catering (extra cost). The skipper handles all navigation and anchoring – you just relax.

Practical tips for Feria week

  • Book early – Feria week is one of Marbella's busiest. Tier A boats often sell out 2–3 weeks ahead.
  • Transport – Puerto Banús is 6 km from the fairground. Taxis cost about €15–20. Uber and Cabify also operate.
  • Weather – June averages 25–30°C, sea temperature 22°C. Evenings are mild but bring a light jacket for the boat.
  • What to wear – Smart casual for the boat; comfortable shoes for the fairground. Ladies often wear flamenco-style dresses for the Feria.
  • Parking – If driving, park at Puerto Banús (paid parking) and taxi to the fairground.

For more ideas, check our guide to Marbella yacht charter Feria San Bernabé 2026.

Other things to do from the boat

If you have a full-day charter, combine the Feria with a coastal cruise. Head west to Cabopino (20 minutes from Puerto Banús) for a swim at the nudist beach or a paella lunch at Chiringuito Cabopino. Alternatively, go east to Estepona (30 minutes) and anchor near the old town. The Mangusta 80's jet ski adds extra fun – you can explore hidden coves like Cala del Faro. All these are within easy reach and make the day feel like a mini-holiday within the Feria.
